source.title: ReLU Neural Networks with Linear Layers Are Biased towards Single- and Multi-index Models
source.authors: Suzanna Parkinson; Greg Ongie; R. Willett

record.file_problem: Full text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether adding input-side linear layers changes generalization and learned network properties, using synthetic single- and multi-index regression rather than the claim versions’ specified settings.
record.gate_note: The paper studies synthetic regression with low-index-rank targets, not random-label memorization or natural-label classification. Out-of-distribution results are excluded because the claim separates them. Reported training-loss and regularization values are not separate rows because they do not test a listed version.
record.test_reason: The study measures how input-side linear layers affect synthetic regression and learned low-dimensional structure. Its results do not test any of V1–V8. Varying depth at fixed width does not test V2, separate Adam and SGD experiments do not test V4's optimizer-performance comparison, and input-gradient spectra do not measure V7's weight-perturbation sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors prove representation-cost and effective-index-rank results and empirically find that input-side linear layers with weight regularization improve generalization when targets have low-dimensional structure, particularly at small or moderate sample sizes. Depth is a tuned hyperparameter. They provide no generalization bounds and caution that their conclusions do not directly extend to deep ReLU networks.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments use synthetic low-index-rank regression targets and add input-side linear layers; they do not test random-label memorization or the claim versions’ specified datasets and interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported generalization and representation-property results depend on architecture (linear layers then ReLU versus shallow or deep ReLU), optimizer (Adam versus a separate SGD experiment), target index rank, label-noise level, training sample count, and effective-rank threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: Validation-tuned input-side linear layers improve in-distribution test MSE on synthetic single- and multi-index regression, with benefits also reported under SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding input-side linear layers with weight regularization can improve generalization on synthetic regression targets with latent low-dimensional structure.

fits_no_version.finding: Networks with input-side linear layers have sharper input-gradient spectral decay, lower effective index rank, and better alignment with the target's central subspace.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input-side linear layers with weight regularization promote learning low-index-rank functions aligned with latent target structure.

fits_no_version.finding: Deep ReLU networks do not outperform shallow networks or reproduce the dramatic input-gradient spectral decay in the tested single-index setting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding nonlinear ReLU layers does not reproduce the benefits of input-side linear layers in these small-scale synthetic regression experiments.

record.peer_reviewed: SIAM Journal on Mathematics of Data Science
record.problems: The experiments use simulated low-index-rank regression data, so their scope does not establish behavior on natural-label classification or random-label memorization. Results are presented mainly in figures without exact values or uncertainty estimates in the supplied text. The authors describe the deep-ReLU experiments as fairly small scale and do not provide generalization bounds.
record.rows_left_out: Out-of-distribution generalization results are excluded because the claim explicitly treats them separately. No additional in-distribution conditions are omitted; the selected rows record the aggregate qualitative findings stated in the text rather than reconstructing separate plotted values.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level held-out performance under random labels.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width needed for interpolation; experimental widths are fixed at 1000.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Comparative held-out performance of adaptive optimizers and SGD under the specified tuning regimes or recovery interventions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on training-set size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The original tests/T2 classification is incorrect for the supplied claim versions. All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8; this does not dispute the reported architectural and spectral findings. No omitted result bears on a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or natural-label classification.
Adam and SGD are used in separate experiments, but the study does not compare their generalization performance as an optimizer test.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison of sharpness with generalization gaps.

rows.subject: networks of the form (4), with extra linear layers
rows.operation_detail: Trained with ℓ2-regularized empirical risk; compared with shallow ReLU networks without linear layers.
rows.baseline: shallow ReLU networks without linear layers; exact values figure only
rows.value: models with extra linear layers demonstrate significantly improved generalization; exact values figure only
rows.note: Aggregate qualitative comparison stated by the authors across the synthetic single- and multi-index settings; figure does not provide recoverable exact values in the supplied text. This is in-distribution regression, not a listed version.
rows.check: The qualitative test-MSE improvement is supported, but it measures no listed version. Depth and regularization strength were selected using validation data; the result concerns this tuned recipe.

rows.subject: networks of the form (4), with extra linear layers
rows.operation_detail: Estimated EGOP singular values using the average gradient outer product on the in-distribution test set.
rows.measure: Singular values of the square root of the estimated AGOP; effective index rank at ε = 10−3
rows.baseline: networks without extra linear layers; exact values figure only
rows.value: networks with extra linear layers have smaller singular values, sharper singular-value dropoff, and smaller effective index rank; exact values figure only
rows.note: The paper describes these as aggregate trends; no exact plotted values are stated in the text.
rows.check: The reported spectral trend is supported, but input-gradient outer-product spectra and effective index rank cannot establish any listed version, including V7.

rows.subject: networks of the form (4), with extra linear layers
rows.operation_detail: Estimated principal-subspace alignment and effective index rank from the AGOP.
rows.measure: Largest principal angle between learned principal subspace and true central subspace; effective index rank
rows.baseline: networks without extra linear layers; exact values figure only
rows.value: models with linear layers demonstrate better alignment, even using the stated generous estimate; exact values figure only
rows.note: The authors also report that models with linear layers have lower effective index rank. The plotted numeric values are not stated in the supplied text.
rows.check: Better principal-subspace alignment and lower effective index rank are supported but measure no listed version. The row combines two distinct measures that should be separated if retained.

rows.subject: networks of the form (4), with extra linear layers
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD instead of Adam; compared with shallow ReLU networks without linear layers.
rows.baseline: shallow networks without extra linear layers; exact values figure only
rows.value: models with extra linear layers demonstrate significantly improved generalization in this setting, even in the presence of label noise; exact values figure only
rows.note: Aggregate qualitative comparison stated by the authors; exact plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: The architectural improvement under SGD is supported. Its baseline is a shallow network trained with SGD, not Adam, so it does not test V4.

rows.subject: networks trained via SGD, with extra linear layers
rows.operation_detail: Estimated singular values and effective index rank from the AGOP.
rows.measure: Singular values and effective index rank
rows.baseline: networks without extra linear layers; exact values figure only
rows.value: models with extra linear layers exhibit sharper singular-value dropoff and smaller effective index rank; exact values figure only
rows.note: The text says the dropoff is less sharp than in models trained with Adam and uses a larger effective-rank tolerance in this setting.
rows.check: The spectral trend is supported but measures no listed version. The larger effective-rank threshold also prevents directly comparing reported effective ranks with the Adam experiment.

rows.subject: deep ReLU models
rows.operation_detail: Compared shallow models, linear-layers-then-ReLU models, and deep ReLU models on single-index data.
rows.baseline: shallow models; exact values figure only
rows.value: deep ReLU models do not perform better than shallow networks; exact values figure only
rows.note: The authors describe these experiments as fairly small scale.
rows.check: The authors explicitly report no improvement over shallow networks, but this is a depth comparison on synthetic regression, not an absence of any V1–V8 effect.

rows.subject: deep ReLU models
rows.operation_detail: Compared EGOP singular-value decay across architectures.
rows.baseline: shallow models; exact values figure only
rows.value: deep ReLU models do not exhibit dramatic singular-value dropoff; exact values figure only
rows.note: The text contrasts this with the dropoff in models with extra linear layers.
rows.check: The authors explicitly report no dramatic spectral dropoff, but this input-gradient measure cannot establish absence of any listed effect.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
